rich_text.plain_text: One of the questions we hear most is: what size print should I get? It's a surprisingly important decision. The wrong size can make a beautiful piece of art look lost on a large wall or cramped in a small space. This guide walks you through the sizes we print, from A3 up to 50 x 70 cm, so you can choose with confidence.

rich_text.plain_text: Living room

text.content: Living room

rich_text.plain_text: The living room is where most people want their most impactful piece. If you're hanging art above a sofa, the general rule is that the artwork should be roughly 60 to 75 per cent of the sofa's width. For a standard three-seater, that means one 50 x 70 as the minimum, and a pair side by side to really own the wall. A single small print above a large sofa will look lost; it's a common mistake that's easily avoided. The

rich_text.plain_text: The tape test: try before you buy

text.content: The tape test: try before you buy

rich_text.plain_text: Here's a trick that interior designers use: cut a piece of paper or newspaper to the exact dimensions of the print size you're considering, and tape it to the wall where you plan to hang the artwork. Live with it for a day or two. You'll quickly get a sense of whether the size feels right for the space, and it costs nothing to test.

text.content: Does the frame change the size?

rich_text.plain_text: Yes, and it's worth accounting for. A frame adds a few centimetres to each side of the print, so if you're fitting art into a specific spot, between two windows, say, or above a piece of furniture with limited clearance, measure with the frame in mind. The frame itself, wood, black or white, is chosen on each product page.

rich_text.plain_text: When in doubt, go bigger

text.content: When in doubt, go bigger

rich_text.plain_text: If you're torn between two sizes, our advice is to go with the larger option. Art that's too small for a space tends to look like an afterthought. A slightly oversized piece, on the other hand, creates intentional impact. It's far more common to regret going too small than too large.
